title: Independent Ethical Assessment of Text Classification Models: A Hate Speech Detection Case Study
benchmark_measurement: Bias assessment in a hate speech detection model related to religious groups (Islam and Christianity). This included analyzing data bias (frequency of terms in hateful vs. non-hateful comments), embedding bias (association of religious terms with neutral words), and classification bias (differences in prediction probabilities for comments about different religions).
models_tested: A custom convolutional neural network (CNN) model using pretrained Stanford GloVe Common Crawl word embeddings
findings: The hate speech detection model exhibited bias related to religion. The training data contained a disproportionate presence of the term 'Islam' in hateful comments compared to 'Christianity'. The model's word embeddings were found to be more biased concerning religious terms than gender terms. Furthermore, a classification bias was identified where the model was more inclined to classify content discussing Islam as hateful compared to similar content about Christianity, a finding supported by a synthetic counterfactual analysis.
